trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out left, around the edge to (5,1) or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
Going around the edge to (1,3), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going around the edge to (1,2), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going up would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going left, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4). So my guess (left from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try around the edge to (5,1).
I can't rule out right or around the edge to (1,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going up would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going around the edge to (1,2), the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,3). So the line goes right.
Going around the edge to (1,3), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2). So the line goes left.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going left would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes down.
The line must go right: left is number 9, which comes later; down is number 10, which comes later.
Going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 5. So the line goes right.
Going right would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going around the edge to (3,1) would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Number 8 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
